subject: babaYagaHut
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs.
Style: Slavic folk art.
reasoning:
I'm scoping out a moderately detailed model, aiming for around 250 parts with concise helper functions, and deciding to keep the hut on chicken legs mostly static without extra joints to simplify the build and reduce risk.

Now I'm sketching out the overall dimensions and structure: a hut roughly 3m wide on 2m-tall legs facing forward, with legs positioned using rods and joint spheres to build the thigh, hock, and foot shape with forward-fanning toes and claws, then starting on the floor platform and log wall layout for the hut body itself.

Walls are built from stacked cylindrical logs in a log-cabin style, with front/back logs running along x and side logs running along z in alternating offsets, colored with varying wood tones to create a natural cabin texture. Working out where the front door opening sits in the log pattern...

Now I'm adding an arched front door with a carved frame, plus ornate folk-art window surrounds with painted red/blue frames around a glowing window. I'm figuring out the gable roof geometry too — calculating the slope angle and plank lengths for the steep slanted roof slabs with ridge height above the eaves.

For the shingles, I'm weighing options: rows of alternating colored strips across each roof side versus adding scalloped edges with small cylinders, but that could balloon into hundreds of parts, so I'm leaning toward simplifying to just colored strip rows without the scallops to keep the part count manageable.

Still building the zigzag outline...

Still working out roof plank orientation...

For the gable, I'm setting a triangular outline with vertical plank lines as thin boxes, then adding a decorative sun emblem with a gold disc and twelve triangular rays as a folk art motif, plus a scalloped carved barge board along the front roof edge.

I want to add a konyok horse-head carving at the ridge pole ends, extruding a simple horse profile at front and back. I'll skip the skull fence idea and instead keep things simple, maybe adding a small front ladder since the hut sits on legs.

Now I'm planning the ladder with slanted rails and rungs leading from the porch platform down to the ground, plus a porch deck extension with railing posts. I also want a crooked stone chimney with a tin cap and a few low-poly smoke puff spheres, and a ring of feather-like cones tilted downward around the hip for the leg's feathered thigh detail.

For the thigh I'm computing feather spikes at varying angles around the leg axis using perpendicular vectors, mixing rufous, cream, and black coloring, plus ellipsoid fluff masses near the pelvis attachment points. I'm keeping the hut symmetrical and picking a palette of warm brown wood tones for the logs.

For the log cabin structure, I'm deciding to keep end caps simple rather than adding discs at every corner, and I'm laying out front/back logs along the x-axis and side logs along the z-axis with slight overhangs at the corners to mimic interlocking joints.

For the door, rather than cutting the logs, I'll keep the front wall logs continuous and mount a decorative raised door panel on top with a frame, giving it a porch-door look, plus add framed windows on the front and sides.

Now I'm working out wall height with eight log courses up to the eaves, then building the gable triangle and roof plane geometry to fit above it with the right slope and apex height.

Working out the shingle row extrusion along the roof slope, placing each row offset upward with slight overlap so the teeth point downward, spacing about 0.34 with height 0.42, giving roughly 7 rows to cover the slope length to the ridge.

I'm cycling through a folk-art palette of teal, red, and ochre for the shingles, nudging each row slightly outward with each step for a layered look, then adding a dark wooden ridge cylinder along the roof peak and starting to shape a decorative "konyok" end-board profile at the gable.

Sketching the horse-head outline points...

Now I'm thinking about mirroring this shape for the back gable end, then adding the decorative sawtooth barge boards (pozaranki) running along the roof rake in red and white stripes.

Working out the sawtooth outline coordinates...

Now I'm positioning the board near the eave, then moving on to a sun emblem for the gable front: a yellow disc with an orange ring behind it and twelve angled cone rays radiating outward to form sun spikes.

For the door, I'm sizing a panel box fitted between the porch deck and wall top, considering whether to add an arched or pointed top, plus a red frame with posts, a lintel, and a kokoshnik-style peaked shape.

I'm adding vertical plank lines, an iron ring handle, and a simple decorative flower motif on the panel—a yellow center with red petals—and thinking through a generic helper function that can orient flowers on any wall face using a basis derived from the surface normal.

Now I'm defining the petal geometry as scaled spheres positioned radially around the center disc, then moving on to planning the window placements along the front and side walls.

For windows, I'm designing a reusable assembly with a glowing pane, cross muntins, a decorative frame, a kokoshnik lintel on top, and teal shutters with flower details — with axis-aware box dimensions so the same function works on both front and side faces.

Still computing face dimensions... Now I'm designing the window component itself: a glowing pane, red side planks and top/bottom boards, dark cross muntins, and a decorative kokoshnik-style crest built with a small extrusion above the lintel.

Teal shutters with little flower ornaments flank each window, and I want to add a decorative frieze band under the eaves with alternating diamonds and triangles for folk-art detail.

I'm also adding a painted fascia along the platform's front and side edges, using small rotated boxes to create a repeating diamond pattern in red, gold, and teal to echo that folk-art styling.

Beyond that, I'm sketching out a porch extension off the front of the deck, complete with railing posts and turned balusters, plus a ladder descending from the porch opening down to the ground with side rails and seven rungs, making sure the foot placement clears the hut's legs.

Now I'm defining the leg geometry for the chicken shape itself, mapping hip, knee, hock, and foot joints per side to get the characteristic forward-bending thigh, backward-angled shin, and forward tarsus that gives a bird its natural stance.

Adding leg and foot details...

I'll alternate two feather colors per ring to add variation, and compute a perpendicular basis for each segment direction, picking a fallback axis when the cross product degenerates. For the body I'm adding fluffy pants at the hip with scaled ellipsoids plus underbelly spheres, and sketching a stone chimney box on the roof's left side.

I'm placing the chimney at the correct height following the roof slope, with brick bands, a cap, and drifting icosahedron smoke puffs that grow as they rise -- keeping total height around 6.6 units. For a fun detail, I'll skip hanging garlic and instead add small skull lanterns atop the porch posts, with glowing orange eye sockets.

Now I'm working out the posts and railing for the porch, plus scattering a few flattened green moss lumps across the roof ridge and eaves for texture. Then I'm figuring out the door placement -- centered on the front wall, sized to fit within the wall height, with red platband posts flanking it and a lintel crest positioned just below the wall top.

I'm fitting the crest extrusion above the lintel and checking it overlaps the logs cleanly on the front face. For the windows, I'm checking spacing so the frames and shutters don't collide with the door frame or poke past the wall corners -- realizing the shutters would overhang past the log corners, so I'm deciding to drop shutters on the front face and just keep the inner frame bright there instead.

Now I'm setting the face offsets for front and side log faces, computing where side logs terminate relative to the front face depth to confirm they stay hidden within it. I'm leaving the back plain with matching gable boards instead of adding a door, and moving on to the next structural loop.

I'm computing roof overhang and gable face positions, then checking where the barge boards and sun decoration sit relative to the gable triangle to make sure the sun's radius and rays fit within the triangle's width at that height.

Since the rays were too small at the top, I'm shrinking the sun disc and ring sizes, and now adding vertical batten boxes to the gable face, computing their height as a function of x position so they stay bounded within the triangle's slope.

Since this is a diorama category, I'm adding a modest round earthen base beneath everything with a slight sink, plus grass tufts and a few mushrooms for scenery, making sure the sink stays within acceptable tolerance.

I'll add grass tufts, a few stones, and keep the scene around 30 parts, with a layered soil/grass base cylinder set at height 0.12. Now I'm setting up the imports and builder helpers to start writing the actual construction code.

Writing helper functions...

Still writing face helpers...

Setting the thickness axis via the up vector, then placing a small center cylinder slightly above the base. I'm defining a window helper and an ogee crest extrusion using an outline swept along the u-axis, plus a sawtooth board function for edge profiles, and now starting a log wall color palette array.

Working out log cylinder placements along front, back, and side edges with alternating colors and radii, checking the stacked height matches the platform top. I'm deciding to skip extra details like moss and end-cap tinting for simplicity, and considering adding an inner box to prevent see-through gaps between the stacked logs.

Now I'm setting up the floor platform as a dark wood box, then planning decorative diamond shapes on the fascia boards along the front and side faces, rotated 45 degrees to create a lattice pattern, and thinking through how to extend the box-drawing helper function to support rotation for these diamonds.

Checking roof overhang clearance against the platform bounds, then working out the porch deck placement—centering it above the fascia line and making sure the deck edges don't awkwardly clip through the diamond pattern on the front face where the two elements overlap in z and y.

I'll skip the diamonds too close to center so the porch's own fascia reads cleanly, then add posts with cylindrical shapes topped by a small skull decoration, plus side rails with balusters while leaving the front open for a ladder. Now I'm laying out the ladder rails and rungs with their coordinates.

For the legs, I'm computing hip, knee, hock, and foot joint positions using scaled offsets, placing a pelvis sphere and working down through drumstick and tarsus segments to the toe base, then spreading the toes forward and at angles while checking they clear the ladder's footprint.

Now I'm defining a capsule-based thigh segment and starting a feather/fluff distribution function that walks along a limb axis, computing perpendicular basis vectors and interpolating radius at each row to scatter feather tufts around the surface.

Still writing fluff function...

After that, I plan to move onto the toe assembly with knuckle spheres and claws built on top of the foot structure.

Claw end lands just below ground level, good. I'm building toes with knuckle and pad spheres, adding backward-pointing spurs on the tarsus, and placing six flattened cylinder rings along the tarsus for scale texture, then defining the color palette with rust, orange, and cream tones.

Now I'm setting up the roof ridge as a cylinder and placing the konyok (gable ornament) outlines at the front and back ends, aligning them atop the ridge with proper height and depth offsets.

Adding the glowing eye detail on each konyok and then moving on to generating the shingle rows using directional vectors for the extrusion per side.

I'm also thinking about barge boards hanging beneath the roof edges at the gable ends, positioned just under the shingle surface so the decorative frieze teeth hang toward the interior and remain visible against the gable triangle behind them.

Now I'm sketching the gable triangle fill planks with battens, plus a sun emblem, then tallying up the total part count across logs, platform, fascia, porch, door, windows, roof shingles, ridge pieces, barge boards, gables, and battens to get a rough budget for the whole structure.

Adding the leg, ring, chimney, and mushroom-base elements to that tally, I land around 450 parts, comfortably under my 1000-part limit, with triangle counts per sphere and spike also staying reasonable.

For the side windows, I'm placing them at offsets along the side face using an origin, up-vector, and outward normal, planning two windows symmetrically spaced along the side wall rather than centered.

Writing window placement function...

Writing door panel code...

Adding door hinges and crest geometry...

Now I'm placing a chimney on the left roof slope, checking that its box position clears the sloped surface so it doesn't float or clip below the roofline at the lower edge.

I'm scattering tufts, mushrooms, and stones around the base radius, placing mushrooms with hemisphere caps and spotted stems near the hut's front corners. I'm making sure the base circle, hut footprint, and ladder all align centered on the model before finalizing and writing the code.

Now I'm working out the spike and rod helper signatures with color options, then writing the foot geometry with toe rods splayed at angles from a central sphere joint.

Still writing toe/claw code...

Still working out diamond box orientation and dimensions per face axis, then moving on to the porch fascia geometry with its own length and offset skip logic.

For the skull decorations, I'm planning a bone-colored sphere head with a jaw box, dark eye sockets holding small glowing orange spheres inside, and a nose spike, all oriented to face forward on the porch. Now shifting to finalizing the code with loose typing for parameters.
